key_insight: MOSAIC is a two-phase, agentic LLM framework that can infer multidimensional disease severity from structured EHR data, using type 2 diabetes as a proof of concept.
clinical_relevance: It could support more nuanced severity phenotyping than rule-based scores, potentially improving risk stratification and research classification in clinical records.
method: Built a two-phase LLM orchestration system for severity phenotyping.
Tested on SyntheticMass T2D cohorts with open-weight and proprietary pipelines.
Compared outputs against three algorithmic severity references and patient outcomes.
evidence_signal: On the abstract’s synthetic cohort, open-weight MOSAIC closely matched the proprietary version (weighted kappa 0.773) and showed moderate-to-fair agreement with existing severity scores while also separating mortality and complication risk.
watch_item: Results are from synthetic data and one disease area, so real-world clinical validation and safety testing are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Multi-Large Language Model Orchestrated Severity Assessment of Clinical Records (MOSAIC)
